quotes.text: You are not eating for tomorrow. You are eating for the person you will be at seventy.
Health is the one thing you cannot buy back later at the price you sold it.
The best time to look after your body was ten years ago. The second best is this evening’s dinner.
Your future self cannot cook today’s dinner. You can.
Every meal is a small deposit into an account you will need decades from now.
The choices that add good years are almost never dramatic. They are the ordinary ones, made again and again.
Someday you will want to climb stairs, lift grandchildren and walk to the market. Start preparing now.
Health is like a garden. Most of the work is small, regular and invisible until it blooms.
A long life is nice. A long life spent able to move, think and enjoy your food is the actual goal.
Bones, muscles and hearts are built quietly, over years, on ordinary meals.
The body keeps a very good record of how it was treated.
It takes decades to earn a strong old age, and every dinner is part of the effort.
Today’s plate is a message to your future self. Make it a kind one.
Nobody thanks their older self for the years they ignored their health. Plenty thank their younger self for the ones they did not.
One meal will not make you healthy. One meal will not make you unwell. The habit is what stays with you.
A slow, steady approach is the only one that has ever reached the finish line.
Aim to be the person who is still cooking, walking and laughing at eighty.
Think of your health as something you build with every meal, not something you fix once a year.
Prevention is quiet and unglamorous, and it is the best deal on offer.
You will not notice most of what you do today for your health. That is how you know it is working.
The years ahead are made of the days you are in now.
Eat for the long run and the short run will often take care of itself.
Give your body good years, not just good days.
There is no finish line. There is only the next good choice, and the one after.
Look after the small things and the big things are less likely to arrive uninvited.
Small steps, repeated for a decade, will out-walk any sprint.
The reward for eating well is mostly invisible: the trouble that never arrived, the energy that stayed.
Ask what your body would like to be able to do in twenty years, then feed it accordingly.
A little patience with your health now saves a lot of impatience later.
Quick fixes fade. Real change is slow, quiet and lasting.
Every healthy elder you admire got there one ordinary meal at a time.
Health is not the absence of a bad day. It is a body that recovers from one.
The next ten years will happen either way. Spend them with a body that is looking after you.
Your body is a long-term partner. Treat it like one.
The goal is not to live forever. It is to live well for as long as you get.
Compound interest works on health too. It just pays out in energy instead of coins.
Nobody has ever looked back at fifty and wished they had eaten less well at forty.
It is never too late to start and never too early to care. Today is a fine day for either.
Five years from now, today’s dinner will not matter. The thousand dinners like it will.
The strongest people you know did not get there in a month. They got there by not quitting for years.
The kind of old age you are hoping for is being built by the kind of Tuesdays you are having.
Your body will be the longest relationship of your life. It is worth investing in.
Do not aim for a perfect year. Aim for a year in which most of the days were kind to your body.
Slow change has one great advantage: it stays.
Whatever you are trying to become, it will be made of what you do repeatedly, starting with breakfast.
